newsitem.title: USA: BPA lowers Thurs peak, firm power $1.00/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA lowers Thurs peak, firm power $1.00/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) lowered firm peak power prices for Thursday by $1.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) and resumed sales of displacement power, the agency said Wednesday.
BPA still offered 300 megawatts of firm peak power, but lowered prices to $13.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest sales and $14.50 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
BPA also offered power at $7.00 per MWh during hours ending 0100-0600 and 2300-2400 PST to buyers willing to displace thermal generation with hydropower.
Prices for non-firm power during shoulder hours on Thursday (0600, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200 PST) were unchanged at $11.00 for Northwest and $12.00 for COB.
Prices for firm and non-firm power during off-peak hours on Thursday were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.
